problem: Generic LLM planners lack robotics expertise and produce infeasible or illogical subgoal plans (missing containers, wrong object quantities, ignoring environment prefixes). Template planners (FILM/Prompter) overfit ALFRED's 7 task types and fail on nomenclature mismatch between instruction and environment objects (e.g., 'table' vs 'desk').
motivation: Daily long-horizon instruction following needs both common-sense generalization and robot-executable, environment-feasible plans. Domain-specific embodied planning data is scarce and ALFRED's crowdsourced labels are noisy (~20%+ errors). Observation: ChatGPT-generated planning data has >60% logic errors unless it is guided to self-correct with templates, and plan failures often stem from object-name mismatch that a semantic map can resolve.
key_idea: Fine-tune Llama on a 67K embodied planning dataset built via ALFRED conversion plus template-feedback self-instruction, and pair it with a segmentation-improved semantic-map skill module and a BERT-similarity Re-Plan that substitutes mismatched subgoal objects.
insight: Ablations show each module matters: replacing RoboPlanner with Prompter's planner drops HLP ACC from 96 to 58 and Generalization HLP ACC from 78 to 0; removing Re-Plan drops SR 60 to 52; removing RoboSkill's improved perception drops SR 60 to 56. Template feedback cuts logical errors in generated data from >60% to 15%. Prompter-planner variants get higher PLWSR because its rule-merged object names avoid exploration, whereas Re-Plan only triggers after extensive search, trading efficiency for real-world applicability.
method: RoboPlanner: Llama-7B supervised fine-tuned (cross-entropy, lr 1e-5, 2 epochs) on 67K embodied planning samples plus 20K generic web data; outputs subgoal phrases matched to robot binaries like 'Pickup Pencil'.

Embodied planning dataset: 60K samples derived from ALFRED (low-level instructions rewritten as subgoal phrases, 7 original + 5 new composed task types via templates) plus 7K ChatGPT self-instruct samples.

Template feedback self-instruction: ChatGPT few-shot generation from 360 seed samples (20 sampled per prompt); template-guided reflection with action/task-type/requirement lists corrects data; remaining 15% errors fixed manually.

RoboSkill: Prompter-style perception/navigation/interaction pipeline; U-Net depth and FastSAM segmentation (trained on 80K ALFRED seen-scene images) build a dynamic 5cm-grid semantic map with pixel-count threshold filtering of reliable objects; dynamic class selection includes goal-related small objects.

Re-Plan: when target not found after exploration, BERT computes similarity between target and confirmed map objects; if the best similarity >0.7, replaces the object in the subgoal (e.g., table→desk), avoiding repeated LLM calls.

setting.backbone: Llama-7B (fine-tuned) planner + FastSAM segmentation + U-Net depth + BERT similarity
setting.training_data: 67K embodied planning data (60K ALFRED-derived/template, 7K ChatGPT self-instruct) + 20K generic Internet data; 80K ALFRED images for segmentation
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (depth predicted by U-Net, segmentation by FastSAM) building a semantic map
setting.action_space: high-level subgoals executed via ALFRED skills (navigation + interaction actions)
setting.privileged: none stated for the main method (baseline reproductions in ablation are given ground-truth object info; LLM-Planner given all scene objects)

results: On ALFRED test unseen with high-level instructions only, RoboGPT reaches SR 55.46 vs Prompter 41.53 and OPEx 41.27; with high+low-level instructions SR 60.76 vs CAPEAM 50.36. On 50 generalization tasks, HLP ACC is 78% vs LLM-Planner 34% and Prompter 0%.
limitations: Evaluation on small hand-selected sets (50 Valid Unseen episodes, 50 generalization tasks); ALFRED labels are noisy (>20% ambiguous high-level instructions).
Re-Plan lowers path-length-weighted efficiency (PLWSR/PLWGC) since it triggers only after extensive exploration; execution/interaction success still lags planning accuracy.
Only simulated in ALFRED; planning is text-only (no multimodal planning) and no real-robot tests.
